speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious to get your perspective on what is unique about leading a company in moments of incredible dynamic change that's very different than leading a company when that's not the case.
zh: 我很好奇,想听听你对在极其剧烈的动态变化时期领导一家公司有什么独特之处,这与在没有这种变化的情况下领导一家公司是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you join and it feels like things are relatively ho-hum for maybe 18 months, then you have the pandemic, then you have Visa M&A, then you have fintech is dead market implosion, and then you have AI.
zh: 所以你加入的时候,感觉事情相对平淡无奇了大概 18 个月,然后你遇到了疫情,然后是 Visa 并购,然后是「金融科技已死」的市场崩盘,然后是 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's unique about running a decent portion of the company in the role of COO through those specific times?
zh: 在这些特定时期以 COO 的角色管理公司的相当大一部分,有什么独特之处?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I feel at least as far as my journey at Platt is concerned, in a weird way, there's nothing unique about it because at almost every step there was something like that.
zh: 所以至少就我在 Platt 的历程而言,说来奇怪,我觉得没有什么独特之处,因为几乎在每个阶段都有类似这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should talk about the three weeks where it wasn't that.
zh: 我们应该聊聊那没有这种事情的三周。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always been things like that.
zh: 这样的事情一直都存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the key is always you just have to be relentlessly focused on kind of still moving the business itself forward.
zh: 我认为关键始终是,你必须毫不松懈地专注于继续推动业务本身向前发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think whether it's in the context of Visa or COVID or anything else, I think one of the things we've always really been very focused on is ruthlessly focusing on making sure that we're serving our customers, we're serving the ecosystem, we'll continue to move the ball forward irregardless of what happens on something like that.
zh: 所以我认为无论是在 Visa 的背景下,还是疫情,还是其他任何事情,我们一直非常专注于的事情之一就是,毫不留情地专注于确保我们在服务客户、服务生态系统,无论发生类似什么样的事情,我们都会继续把球往前推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a couple of tactical ways in which I think we did that.
zh: 所以有几种战术层面的方式,我认为我们是这样做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think one is just in terms of how we speak to the company.
zh: 你知道,我认为其中之一就是我们如何与公司沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very clear that this was just like one potential milestone upon many.
zh: 我们非常明确,这只是许多潜在里程碑中的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not the end goal.
zh: 它不是最终目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not the finish line.
zh: 它不是终点线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's particularly important, even if like, you know, you see companies now going public and so forth.
zh: 我认为这一点特别重要,即使,你知道,你现在看到公司在上市等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I learned a lot there from my days at Square, where that's kind of how Sarah and Jack talked about the IPL, right?
zh: 我认为我在 Square 的日子里从中学到了很多,因为 Sarah 和 Jack 谈到 IPL 时就是那种方式,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't the finish line.
zh: 它不是终点线。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just another milestone amongst many milestones.
zh: 它只是众多里程碑中的又一个里程碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you take that attitude,
zh: 我认为如果你持那种态度,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier to remain focused.
zh: 保持专注就会更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is the way you think about the team.
zh: 第二个是你如何看待团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we've always tried to kind of minimize the number of folks that are kind of truly actively working on something like that, right?
zh: 我认为我们一直试图把真正积极参与这类事情的人数降到最低,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in the case of COVID, obviously that's a little bit different.
zh: 比如在疫情的情况下,显然那有点不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: That affects everybody.
zh: 那影响所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the case of Visa, the team that was actively day-to-day working on the transaction was actually quite small.
zh: 但在 Visa 的情况下,日复一日积极参与这笔交易的团队实际上相当小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone else was 100% focused on continuing to grow the business.
zh: 而其他所有人都 100% 专注于继续发展业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were certainly aware of the transaction, aware of what was happening.
zh: 他们当然知道这笔交易,知道正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, how could you not be, given some of the press at the time?
zh: 而且显然,考虑到当时的媒体报道,你怎么可能不知道呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: But fundamentally, like they were 100% focused on their day job on, you know, again, serving our customers, serving consumers, like building the platform and the ecosystem.
zh: 但从根本上说,他们 100% 专注于自己的日常工作,你知道,再次强调,服务我们的客户,服务消费者,比如建设平台和生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think it's mainly sort of a comms kind of a thing where you're just sort of relentlessly landing those messages?
zh: 你觉得这主要是某种沟通层面的事情吗,就是你只是不断地传递那些信息?

speaker: Unknown
en: So is it just narrative and storytelling and keeping people focused sort of in the way that you communicate?
zh: 所以说到底就是叙事和讲故事,并通过你沟通的方式来让人们保持专注?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or are there other things that you have to do?
zh: 还是你必须做其他一些事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think it's substantive as well, right?
zh: 我的意思是,我认为它也是实质性的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, in this case, I don't know if I would think of it as kind of falling apart.
zh: 我的意思是,在这个案例中,我不知道我会不会把它看作某种崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, certainly the deal didn't go through, but then subsequently, right, like we raised at a significant upround, we provided liquidity to our team, right?
zh: 我的意思是,当然这笔交易没有通过,但随后,对吧,比如我们以显著上调的估值进行了融资,我们为团队提供了流动性,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so suddenly from an employee's perspective,
zh: 所以突然之间,从员工的角度来看,

speaker: Unknown
en: You're actually pretty happy about, right?
zh: 你其实相当高兴,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, I think that went a long way to kind of show the intent for what we're trying to build.
zh: 所以,你知道,我认为这对展示我们想要构建的东西的意图起了很大作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's about just like the culture and like what you really value at the end of the day, right?
zh: 我认为这关乎文化,以及归根结底你真正看重什么,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you build a company around like, you know, any given milestone, like an acquisition or an IPO or something like that, I think it's really hard to build like a truly great company.
zh: 我认为如果你围绕任何一个给定的里程碑来构建公司,比如一次收购或一次 IPO 或类似的事情,我认为要构建一家真正伟大的公司是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus if you build a company and a culture, like focused on actually kind of delivering for your customers, delivering for the, in our case, like the ecosystem that we're building, like I genuinely think our teams, certainly I do, believe in that, right?
zh: 相反,如果你构建的公司和文化专注于真正为你的客户交付,为——在我们的案例中——我们正在构建的生态系统交付,我是真心认为我们的团队,至少我是,相信这一点,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we believe in that like much more than we believe in like any one of these kind of externalities that might happen.
zh: 而且我们相信这一点,远胜于我们相信任何一种可能发生的外部事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as a result, it makes it easier to kind of stay focused, right?
zh: 我认为结果是,这让保持专注变得更容易,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it doesn't just start when that event happens.
zh: 所以它并不是在那个事件发生时才开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you're constantly talking about what you're trying to do for the ecosystem as a whole and for your customers and so forth and so on.
zh: 而是你一直在不断谈论你想为整个生态系统、为你的客户等等做些什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not like it's a new thing versus I think to me, sometimes if you think if you frame it more as like a comms thing,
zh: 所以它不是一件新事情,而我认为,对我来说,有时如果你把它更多地框定为一种沟通层面的事情,

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds a little bit more like it was reactive to just that moment, right?
zh: 它听起来就更像是只是对那一刻的被动反应,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus, no, this was always the culture that we were building.
zh: 而事实是,不,这一直是我们构建的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It never changed, right?
zh: 它从未改变过,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the really great companies, they've been able to do that.
zh: 我认为真正伟大的公司,他们能够做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've been able to maintain that focus, to maintain that culture over kind of a very long period of time, irregardless of what happens.
zh: 他们能够保持那种专注,保持那种文化,在相当长的一段时间里,无论发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's what then builds the resiliency to handle all the ups and downs that you talked about.
zh: 而我认为这正是建立起韧性的关键，让你能够应对你刚才谈到的所有起起伏伏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's very rare that you find a company where it's really just straight up into the right.
zh: 比如，你很少能找到一家公司是一路直线上扬、毫无波折的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you pick that apart a little bit and you talk about sort of building the foundational culture that to the point that you're making kind of becomes that ballast through all the ups and downs of the company's life, how do you think about what it actually means to create or construct or build that, you know, the idea of being customer centric, sort of all the sort of underpinnings that sort of drive the culture?
zh: 那么，如果你稍微拆解一下这一点，谈谈构建那种基础性的文化——就你所说的观点而言，它会成为公司整个生命周期中所有起伏的压舱石——你如何看待「以客户为中心」这样的理念，以及那些驱动文化的底层基础，究竟意味着什么？如何去创造、构建或打造它？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you pick it apart and you use sort of the least generic culture-y language, how do you actually go about doing it in your eyes?
zh: 如果你把它拆开，用最不空泛的文化类语言来说，在你看来，实际上要怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the first step is always, this is obvious, right?
zh: 我认为第一步总是——这很显而易见，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But you actually have to take the time to think about it and kind of formalize it in a way, right?
zh: 但你实际上必须花时间去思考它，并以某种方式把它正式化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's something you just want to kind of leave to chance.
zh: 我不认为这是你想要听天由命、放任自流的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a lot to be said for, again, I think the founders, like Zach and others, like I think he was very deliberate about the kind of culture that he wanted to build.
zh: 而且我认为这很能说明问题，再说了，我认为创始人，比如 Zach 和其他人，我想他对想要建立什么样的文化是非常有意识的、深思熟虑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've seen a lot of founders that they're not.
zh: 而我见过很多创始人并不是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just kind of an afterthought, right?
zh: 那只是一种事后才想起来的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of the result of everything else that's happening around them versus like, no, this is like, I'm proactively thinking about what I want it to be and what I'm aiming for.
zh: 它更像是周围其他一切事情发生后的结果，而不是说，不，这是我在主动思考我希望它成为什么样子、我的目标是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think once you have that, I think the second piece is you have to hire for it.
zh: 我认为一旦你有了这个，我认为第二点就是你必须围绕它来招人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to be willing to make actual trade-offs, right?
zh: 所以你必须愿意做出真正的取舍，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of the kinds of people that you're bringing on board, particularly in leadership positions, but really across the entire organization, right?
zh: 在你要引进什么样的人这方面，尤其是在领导岗位上，但实际上是贯穿整个组织的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think you have to build out a rewards structure around that as well.
zh: 然后我认为你还必须围绕它建立一套奖励结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it has to matter for who gets promoted, who doesn't, who gets a raise, who doesn't, who gets more equity, who doesn't.
zh: 所以它必须对谁升职、谁不升职、谁加薪、谁不加薪、谁拿到更多股权、谁拿不到产生影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things have to be tied not just purely to results, but to an individual's ability to enhance and further and contribute to the culture as well.
zh: 这些事情必须不仅仅与结果挂钩，还要与一个人提升、推进和贡献文化的能力挂钩。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you found have been the trickiest moments around culture or when it has been the most tested in your eyes?
zh: 在你看来，围绕文化最棘手的时刻是什么时候？或者说它在什么时候经受的考验最大？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the hardest is always when there's a clear kind of conflict between the culture and some short-term goal.
zh: 我认为最难的时候总是当文化和某个短期目标之间存在明显冲突的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so where you believe in the culture long-term, you know what's right, but in the short-term, there's a shortcut that would clearly maybe lead to better metrics or a better operational outcome, that becomes very challenging.
zh: 也就是说，长期来看你相信文化，你知道什么是对的，但短期来看，有一条捷径，显然可能带来更好的指标或更好的运营结果，这就变得非常有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's where, again, I think the really good leaders, they are able to maintain that discipline and maintain that focus on kind of that long-term North Star vis-à-vis letting themselves, like I said earlier, to get distracted and say, no, no, look, I know I can get to this one specific milestone.
zh: 而我认为正是在这里，再强调一次，真正优秀的领导者能够保持那种自律，保持对那种长期北极星的专注，而不是像前面说的那样让自己分心，说：不，不，听着，我知道只要做几个妥协，我就能更快到达这个特定的里程碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a little bit quicker if I just make a few compromises.
zh: 只要我做几个妥协，就会快那么一点点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that ever ends there.
zh: 我不认为那条路会就此打住。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you go down that path and the folks around you see that, there's going to be a second time, there's going to be a third time, there's going to be a fourth time.
zh: 一旦你走上那条路，而周围的人看到了这一点，就会有第二次、第三次、第四次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And before you know it, those cultural principles don't really stand for much of anything anymore.
zh: 而且不知不觉间，那些文化原则就不再有什么实际意义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty clear that the short term has overtaken the long term.
zh: 很明显，短期已经压倒了长期。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about things like, you know, you have a star employee in some dimension, but they're an asshole or they violate your culture in some way, but they're really high performing.
zh: 那这样的事情呢，比如说，你在某个维度上有一个明星员工，但他们是个混蛋，或者他们以某种方式违反了你的文化，但他们绩效真的很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you find like there are those tension points quite often or very rarely?
zh: 你觉得这种张力点是经常出现，还是很少见？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, those happen, right?
zh: 我是说，这种情况确实会发生，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're the key is you just have to be...
zh: 我认为关键在于，你必须做到……

speaker: Unknown
en: Very open, honest, and direct, right?
zh: 非常开放、诚实和直接，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you just have to take that on right away.
zh: 所以你必须立刻正视这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I certainly think, I think that's a conversation I've had with a lot of folks over the years.
zh: 我当然认为，这些年来我和很多人都有过这样的谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the key there is always to make sure that you're really discerning kind of intent, right?
zh: 我认为其中的关键始终是要真正辨别对方的意图，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a version of the world where you might be acting in what like I or our culture perceives to be like an asshole, but you're not actually doing it on purpose, right?
zh: 因为存在这样一种情况：你的行为方式在像我或我们的文化看来像个混蛋，但你实际上并不是故意的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's simply me coming to you and saying, hey,
zh: 所以这只是我来找你说，嘿，

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really being perceived as you being an asshole.
zh: 这真的让人觉得你是个混蛋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like maybe if you tried it a little bit differently, we would get to a much better outcome together.
zh: 比如，如果你稍微换个方式，我们一起可能会得到好得多的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you say that to people, the vast majority of people I've ever worked with, their reaction to this is, hey, Eric, thank you.
zh: 一旦你对人说了这些，我共事过的绝大多数人，他们的反应都是：嘿，Eric，谢谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really appreciate you caring about me enough to give me that feedback.
zh: 我真的很感激你足够在乎我，愿意给我这样的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they do their best to course correct.
zh: 然后他们会尽最大努力去纠正方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it might not be instantaneous, but over a period of time, you know, they evolve in terms of like how they interact with their team and kind of the rest of the organization and that solves.
zh: 这可能不是立竿见影的，但经过一段时间，他们在与团队以及组织其他成员互动的方式上会逐渐转变，问题就解决了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And somebody that was supposed to be an asshole two years ago suddenly is like just crushing it from a culture perspective.
zh: 一个两年前本该是个混蛋的人，突然从文化的角度来看变得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And swinging gears a little bit, you know, because you've been at the company for a long time, you've seen it go from a relatively small company to a relatively large company or certainly a larger company.
zh: 然后稍微换个话题，因为你在公司待了很久，你见证了它从一家相对较小的公司变成一家相对较大的公司，或者至少是一家更大的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The natural thing that happens when you add more and more people and you grow is you end up with more bureaucratic organizations.
zh: 当你不断增加人手、不断成长时，自然而然会发生的事情就是，你最终会得到更加官僚化的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in almost always cases, there's some form of slowness that's introduced into a company.
zh: 但在几乎所有情况下，公司会被引入某种形式的迟缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of your observations about that and sort of the organism that is the company as it's evolved?
zh: 关于这一点，以及关于公司这个有机体随时间演化的过程，你有哪些观察？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a few things.
zh: 我认为有这么几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, so one, I think generally speaking, I do think it's true that the bigger you get, the harder it gets, right?
zh: 我是说，第一，总体而言，我确实认为公司越大，事情就越难，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, like the bigger you get, the more assets you have at your disposal to kind of fight that off, right, in a way.
zh: 但与此同时，公司越大，你手上可用来对抗这种趋势的资产也越多，从某种意义上说是这样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think there's a few kind of core things that I think I and we do.
zh: 所以我认为有几件核心的事情,是我以及我们所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one is making sure that even as you get bigger, you're always crystal clear on who the decision maker actually is.
zh: 我认为其中之一是,即使你变得更大了,也要始终非常清楚地知道,真正的决策者到底是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you don't want to live in a world where, you know, it's unclear.
zh: 而且我认为你不会想生活在一个……你知道,情况不清晰的世界里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have five, six, seven people.
zh: 你有五、六、七个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all think they're the ones ultimately kind of making the final decisions.
zh: 他们都认为自己是最终拍板做决定的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think even on something as mundane as just going through my leadership meetings or going through any meetings, just being crystal clear at the end, like what are the things we're actually going to go do?
zh: 所以我认为,哪怕是在像我过领导层会议或者参加任何会议这样平凡的事情上,也要在最后非常清楚地明确,我们真正要做的事情是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: But also then crucially, like who's on point to do it and trying

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后第二个，我，我们，我们被专业性迷住了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so

speaker: Unknown

en: It actually hasn't existed before.
zh: 它以前实际上从未存在过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's pockets where you could talk yourself into thinking that, hey, this person actually has done it before.
zh: 但我认为会有一些局部情况让你说服自己相信，嘿，这个人以前真的做过这件事。

zh: 而在一个你不断应对某种不确定性的世界里，对吧，说“你知道吗，我很想让这个人加入我的团队”总是非常有吸引力的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That is better than me at looking around corners because they've kind of done it before.
zh: 因为他们在提前预判方面比我强，因为他们差不多做过这件事。

zh: 而且这可以发生在任何层级，对吧？

zh: 可以非常具体，比如，我该怎么搭建一个企业销售团队？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I was a consultant myself, so I don't mean this as a diss, but I think it's, like,
zh: 你知道，我自己也当过顾问，所以我不是在贬低他们，但我认为这更像是，

speaker: Unknown

zh: 他们更适合在短期内当一个好顾问，在某种程度上帮你交付，而不是那个真正能帮你把业务建立起来的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, because again, anybody that you put into that situation for the next 18 months is going to end up sounding just like that person at the end of that 18 month period, except now they have all these other amazing qualities, right, that make them awesome.
zh: 因为，因为再说一次，任何你放进那个位置的人，接下来 18 个月结束时，最终听起来都会和那个人一样，只是现在他们还具备了所有这些其他了不起的品质，对吧，让他们很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus this person, it's like, if they don't have the rest,
zh: 而对比这个人，就像是，如果他们不具备其余的部分，

speaker: Unknown

zh: 那么你当初招人时感知到的那个优势，实际上会随着时间被侵蚀，因为反正它会被身处那个职位的人复制出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's been your observation as the difference between a very senior exec and a founder?
zh: 作为观察，一个非常资深的高管和一个创始人之间的区别是什么？

en: Like not just the role, obviously, the difference between a CEO and a COO, but is it there's some moral authority that comes with being a founder that's just different?
zh: 不只是角色，显然，CEO 和 COO 之间的区别，而是创始人身上是否有某种道德权威，是不一样的？

zh: 还是说有一种内在的风险偏好和押上整个业务的意愿，是不一样的？

zh: 或者你认为人们在某种程度上过度纠结于做创始人相对于 CEO 或 COO 意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, no, I definitely think there's a difference.
zh: 嗯，不，我确实认为有区别。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我觉得它可以是双向的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?

en: So I don't think it's as simple as it's always good.

en: I think sometimes it can be, it can be bad.

speaker: Unknown
en: The good founders, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the one thing that they have, which is impossible to replicate, is truly fundamentally their baby.
zh: 我觉得他们拥有的、无法复制的一件事，就是这真的是他们从根本上的亲生孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in the same way that like, look, I love my kids in a certain way, you love your kids in a certain way.
zh: 就像，你看，我以一种特定的方式爱我的孩子，你以一种特定的方式爱你的孩子。

en: You will never love my kids the way you love your own, and I will never love your kids the way, no matter how awesome they are, no matter how much time I spend with them, no matter how well-intentioned I am, it's almost impossible to do that, right?
zh: 你永远不会像爱你自己的孩子那样爱我的孩子，我也永远不会像，无论他们多出色，无论我花多少时间和他们在一起，无论我多么善意，这几乎是不可能的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我甚至可能永远不会像 Williams 至今那样爱它。

zh: 这是对他们的证明，但这也只是这种处境的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just allows you to do things that just become incredibly difficult to do over and over every single day if you don't have that.

en: And so there's nothing that they're not willing to do.
zh: 所以没有什么事情是他们不愿意去做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gives you a level of resilience.

en: That nobody you ever hire is ever going to have.

zh: 答案会是否定的。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the founders that never quit, right?
zh: 而关键就在于那些从不放弃的创始人,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's like the only person that could have made it through all those trials and tribulations to develop the skills that he now has because he's the only person that loved the thing like enough to where like none of that like ever made him question for even a second like whether or not like it's worth it, right?
zh: 所以他是唯一那个能够挺过所有那些考验和磨难、并发展出他现在所拥有的技能的人,因为他是唯一那个热爱这件事到了这种程度的人,以至于那些东西从来没有让他哪怕有一秒钟去怀疑这是否值得,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而他们深深地、深深地尊重这一点,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我丝毫都不怀疑他所做的一切,他可能是错的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think all the really, really great founders, they have that in common.
zh: 而且我认为所有真正、真正优秀的创始人,他们在这一点上是共同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess those things probably haven't changed very much in seven and a half years.
zh: 我猜这些东西在七年半里可能没怎么变。

zh: 但如果把以前的自己和今天的自己相比,有没有几件非常重要的事,会是最显著的?

zh: 我觉得有一件事是伴随着阅历、年龄,或者随你怎么称呼而来的,对吧?

en: Right?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 或者像一个 plaque 还可以更好。

zh: 而且以一种奇怪的方式,比如前几天我和某人聊到这个,我说,我不知道我是否愿意把这种东西强加给我孩子,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in a way, like you want your kids to just be like, look, I achieved this thing and I'm now super happy.
zh: 比如说,某种程度上,你希望你的孩子就是那种,看,我达成了这个东西,我现在超级幸福。

speaker: Unknown

en: And I don't know that I will ever feel that, right?
zh: 而我不知道我自己是否会感受到那种感觉,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Better, better, better, better, better.

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the one hand, I love that.

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't trade it for the world.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但另一方面,比如,我认为你必须得有点疯狂,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 意思是你在七年半的时间里不断累积这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I look at you seven and a half years ago and today every day trying to get a little bit better.
zh: 我看你七年半前和今天,每天努力变得更好一点点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like where is it most substantially expressed?
zh: 比如它最显著地体现在哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest area is probably like in like how I try to show up for my team, right?
zh: 我认为最大的领域大概是,比如在我如何努力为我的团队展现自己这方面,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's where I've grown a lot.
zh: 我认为那是我成长了很多的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I don't know that I've gotten that much better at like selling to customers or doing some of like the tactical things of the job, but I think, you know, how I show up for my team, like how I try to put them in a position to succeed.
zh: 比如,我不认为我在向客户销售或做工作中一些战术性的事情上进步了那么多,但我认为,你知道,我如何为我的团队展现自己,比如我如何努力把他们放在能成功的位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Share more, like, what does that look like?
zh: 多分享一些,比如,那看起来是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, I think that's where those folks would say I've come, come the furthest, right?
zh: 我认为,我认为那正是那些人会说我是进步,进步最大的地方,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the things we talked about.
zh: 就是我们谈到过的那些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hey, how much time are we really kind of spending for those folks that really need it?
zh: 比如,嘿,我们到底花了多少时间给那些真正需要它的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: How far ahead are we thinking in terms of putting these folks in a position to succeed?
zh: 我们在把这些人放在能成功的位置上方面想得多远?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have so many people at Plaid that have internally kind of shot through the ranks that have gone from IC roles to now running $100 million businesses.
zh: 而且我们在 Plaid 有那么多人是内部一路晋升上去的,他们从 IC 岗位做到现在管理一亿美元的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could literally name seven or eight people on my team that have kind of followed that path.
zh: 我真的可以点名我团队里七八个走上了这条路径的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not like every single person kind of always works out, but they've worked out to a phenomenal kind of percentage, right?
zh: 而且不是说每个人都总能成,但他们成过的比例惊人地高,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And they themselves are like so much of the reason for why we've had the success that we've had.
zh: 而他们自己就是我们已经取得的成功的一大部分原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's like, you know, it's picking the right people, but then also then like really kind of being committed to investing in them and giving them that confidence to like say, hey, like, I'm not going to just turn around and take you out of the game, right?
zh: 所以就是,你知道,挑对的人,但然后也真正致力于对他们投资,给他们那种信心,让他们敢于说,嘿,比如,我不会因为你投丢一球就转身把你换下场,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you miss one shot.
zh: 比如如果你投丢了一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's not how this is gonna go down, right?
zh: 事情不会是那样发展的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I genuinely believe in you, right?
zh: 比如我是真心相信你的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can absolutely do this.
zh: 比如你绝对能做到这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna put the team around you to kind of make you shine and then let's go.
zh: 我会围绕你配置团队来让你发光,然后我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you stick with that for long enough,
zh: 而我认为如果你坚持这一点足够久,

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you're just going to be right a high percentage of the time that you're going to end up with like these amazing outcomes, right?
zh: 你知道,你只是在高比例的时间里会是对的,你最终会得到这些了不起的结果,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And they deserve really all the credit for that.
zh: 而功劳真的全都该归他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that again, it's like, there's lots of sports analogies in there, like where you too, oftentimes you'll see coaches, right?
zh: 但再说一次,这里面有很多体育类比,比如你们俩, oftentimes 你会看到教练,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like yank a player, like after the first bout and then surprise, surprise, like they're not going to be very good.
zh: 就像把一名球员换下场，比如在第一节之后就换下，然后呢，毫不意外，他们不会表现得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then everyone else.
zh: 然后是其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just never going to work.
zh: 这永远行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or the next time even they get in, they're just like panicked about like doing the same thing that just got them yanked the first time.
zh: 或者下一次即便他们上场了，他们也只会因为害怕再次犯下上次刚让他们被换下的错误而惊慌失措。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they go to a different team and a different coach.
zh: 然后他们去了一支不同的球队、遇到一位不同的教练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that coach just like, Hey, you got this.
zh: 那位教练就说，嘿，你行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll leave you in, you make a couple mistakes, and then like a quarter of the season in, they're suddenly killing it, right?
zh: 我会让你留在场上，你犯几个错误没关系，然后比如赛季过了四分之一，他们突然就大杀四方了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you see that over and over and over again.
zh: 我觉得你会一次又一次又一次地看到这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, I think tied to that probably also is this notion of like, I just have very little FOMO, right?
zh: 所以，你知道，我觉得与此相关的可能还有这么一点，就是我几乎没有 FOMO（错失恐惧），对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like once I make a decision, like that somebody is like the person I'm gonna invest in, like I'm not that worried about what the other option is or the other option is or the other option is, like I'm then dedicated to kind of seeing it through.
zh: 就像一旦我做出了决定，认定某人是我要投资的人，我就不太担心别的选项是什么，或者别的选项、别的选项是什么，我就会致力于把它坚持到底。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless they give me some really clear reason for saying, hey, like, this just isn't going to work.
zh: 除非他们给我一些非常明确的理由说，嘿，这样根本行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then obviously like, you know, Plaid as a whole comes first, but the bar for that is like pretty high.
zh: 然后显然，你知道，Plaid 作为整体是第一位的，但那个门槛是相当高的。

speaker: Unknown
en: To wrap up, at some point when you're retired or you're not at Plaid or doing something else, what is it you want the people that you worked most closely to say about you?
zh: 收尾环节，在某个时候，当你退休了、或者不在 Plaid 了、在做别的事情，你希望你工作关系最密切的人怎么评价你？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one that like, we really try to do our very best to serve consumers and our customers.
zh: 我觉得第一是，我们真的尽最大努力去服务消费者和我们的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's really important to me, right?
zh: 我觉得这对我真的很重要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This notion that like the work we did actually in many, many, many small ways, in some medium ways, and maybe even fewer big ways, like helped move things forward to be better, right?
zh: 就是这种想法：我们做的工作真的在许许多多小的方面、在一些中等的方面、或许在更少的大的方面，帮助推动事情变得更好，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by that, I mean, there's literally gonna be millions and millions of consumers that will never know my name, but their life will just be a little bit better because of the products and solutions that we brought to market because of the ecosystem that we built.
zh: 我的意思是，字面上说，会有数以百万计的消费者永远不会知道我的名字，但他们的生活会因为我们推向市场的产品和解决方案、因为我们构建的生态系统而变得更好一点点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that goes a long way, right?
zh: 而这意义重大，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot of things you can do in life where like at the end of the day, you look back and it didn't really leave much of a dent.
zh: 我觉得生活中有很多事情，到头来你回头看，它并没有留下多大的印记。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's the first one.
zh: 所以我觉得这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the second one is that I think the people that worked with me, but particularly I think the people that worked for me, right?
zh: 然后第二点是，我觉得那些和我共事过的人，但尤其是那些曾在我手下工作的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like feel like they got as close to their full potential as they could have gotten to, right?
zh: 会觉得他们尽可能地接近了自己的全部潜力，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the second one.
zh: 我觉得这是第二点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that they loved it every minute of every day or anything like that.
zh: ——修正：[[875]] 只是，如果他们真的回想起来会说，嘿，我当年是不是可以去别的地方并且取得更多成就？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like, if they really think back and they're like, hey, could I have gone somewhere else and that kind of achieved more?
zh: 就像是,如果他们真的回过头想,会觉得,嘿,我当初是不是本可以去别的地方、并且取得更多成就?

speaker: Unknown
en: And like in their minds, like the answer is no.
zh: 而在他们心里，答案是没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, Eric and Claude helped me get to a place that like, otherwise I would have gotten to.
zh: 就像，Eric 和 Claude 帮我到达了一个否则我不会到达的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I've always had like folks like that in my life, right?
zh: 我觉得我人生中一直有这样的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like whether it's like, you know, like folks like Michael Mankins at Bain or like Francoise at Square or Eyal at BlueMine and now Zach and others at Square.
zh: 比如像 Bain 的 Michael Mankins，或者 Square 的 Francoise，或者 BlueMine 的 Eyal，以及现在 Square 的 Zach 和其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I've always really, really been lucky.
zh: 我一直真的、真的非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, at Plaid, I've always really been lucky that I've been surrounded by people like that where like, you know, did I enjoy every single moment?
zh: 我是说，在 Plaid，我一直非常幸运能被这样的人们围绕着，就像，你知道吗，我享受每一个瞬间了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no, right?
zh: 不，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But do I believe like they helped me get as close to like my full potential as I probably gotten to?
zh: 但我是否相信他们帮助我尽可能接近了我的全部潜力，接近我大概能达到的程度？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that would mean a lot.
zh: 我觉得那会意义重大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Beautiful place to end.
zh: 很美的收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for the time.
zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Appreciate it.
zh: 很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really appreciate it.
zh: 我真的很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was wonderful.
zh: 那太棒了。
